target_customer: Independent pharmacies in Germany, with consumers as the second side of the platform
problem: German pharmacies are mostly single owner businesses without online ordering, while e-prescription rules required them to take and fill prescriptions digitally from January 2023. Sanvivo gave them software and delivery through partner apps.
business_model: Multisided platform with commission on orders routed through third party delivery partners, plus pharmacy software

founders.name: Julius Rachor
education: Physics degree and PhD in electrical engineering
founders.background_notes: Worked on e-mobility projects and data and ML infrastructure for autonomous driving at BMW, per YC page.

founders.name: Nikolai Alemi Hariri
education: Pharmacist, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
founders.background_notes: His father runs Senftenauer Apotheke in Munich where the idea started, per the company site. The YC page lists him as co-founder and CEO on his profile.

founders.name: Dominic Haul
education: Diploma in Technical Physics, University of Applied Sciences Munich

founders.name: Sven Wildermann
education: Studied computer science in Berlin, no degree listed

competitors.name: gesund.de
competitors.what: Platform linking patients to local pharmacies, including e-prescription redemption
competitors.funding_then: Joint venture of Phoenix Group and Noventi, founded 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Order intake, integration with several pharmacy management systems (ADG, noventi, CGM, Pharmatechnik) and healthcare compliance for e-prescriptions were standard but regulated engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Pharmacy system integrations helped, but the business depended on delivery partners and on regulation that decided who could handle e-prescriptions, and well funded rivals were backed by large wholesalers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger pharmacy platforms backed by wholesalers and mail order incumbents won the e-prescription channel. Sanvivo ended its delivery partnership with Lieferando and Wolt on 31 August 2024.

market_need_then: German e-prescription rollout started in January 2023 and many single owner pharmacies had no online order capability (YC description). Third party pharmacy delivery players Kurando (shut 2022) and Aponia (insolvent 2023) already struggled, per Pharmazeutische Zeitung.

branding.domain_note: Company site is sanvivo.eu, an EU domain rather than a .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and sales oriented toward pharmacists, for example start today and get first orders tomorrow

branding.brand_signature: Consumer app named Vivoly, later removed from app stores

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press in Germany covered the company, but no source shows consumer pull. The consumer app Vivoly was withdrawn in 2024.

pivots.from: Pharmacy delivery and e-prescription marketplace through Lieferando and Wolt
pivots.to: Software for pharmacies, with channel integration portal
pivots.why: CEO cited a changed market and the Digital-Gesetz (DigiG) and its interpretation, which left no sustainable economics for the delivery model

outcome_analysis: Sanvivo launched around the 2023 German e-prescription rollout, linking pharmacies to delivery apps. On 16 August 2024 it told partner pharmacies that its Lieferando and Wolt delivery service would end on 31 August, citing the DigiG law and market changes, and its Vivoly app left the app stores. The company stays Active and sells software to pharmacies, with its site now claiming over 1,000 partner pharmacies. Whether the software pivot has worked is not independently verified.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators (SeedTable, VCBacked, CB Insights, Nordic9) list $500K pre-seed in April 2023 or $1M seed on 26 May 2023 with Heal Capital and Y Combinator, with no press release found, so no round is recorded. Business Punk says the first product was bootstrapped as a side project. Founding year 2021 per YC and company site, 2022 per CB Insights. HQ Munich per YC, Weil per VCBacked. The 1,000 pharmacy figure is unverifiable per Pharmazeutische Zeitung. The status in the directory is Active, so exit is none, but the original business model ended in 2024. Completeness pass: the pre-seed rests on SeedTable and FundedIQ (CB Insights dates a $500K convertible note 2023-01-01) and the $1M seed on Nordic9 alone. The two may overlap; amounts are not summed. Totals elsewhere conflict (537K Standout, 1.0M VCBacked, 1.5M Nordic9). No press release found.
